stories.headline: GPT-6 Astra is rolling out to $20 ChatGPT Plus — and it is OpenAI's first Critical cyber model
stories.why_read: This morning's AI distribution story: Plus access, ARC-AGI-3 99.9%, ExploitBench 100%, API at $10/$50.
body: OpenAI has begun rolling GPT-6 Astra out to ChatGPT Plus subscribers paying $20 a month, after Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium got it from September 3. The company said on X that it may take a few days to reach Plus and Business, and access has been uneven — some people seeing it in ChatGPT Work before regular Chat. Free-tier access has not been announced.

Astra's computer-use pitch is the qualitative jump Greg Brockman called 'very accurate, efficient, and reliable.' Reported scores: 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 in Adapter Harness mode versus 7.8% for GPT-5.6 and 30.2% for Claude Opus 5; 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4; 100% on ExploitBench. That last result is why OpenAI rated it Critical on its Preparedness Framework for cybersecurity and gated the sensitive capabilities. API pricing is $10 / $50 per million tokens, about 2.5× GPT-5.6 Sol. Treat benchmarks as OpenAI's and the press's.

stories.headline: Tesla: talk to Grok to control Cybercab — climate, YouTube, music, destination
stories.why_read: Robotaxi's cabin-software pitch for a steering-wheel-free car, now that Austin public rides are live.
body: Tesla's Robotaxi account posted a one-liner — 'Talk to Grok to control your Cybercab' — quoting a cabin demo of natural-language control for climate, YouTube, and music, plus a phone notification to edit the destination. TeslaNorth notes Tesla did not add a timeline, market list, or software version, so it is not confirmed that every public Austin Cybercab has the voice stack yet.

It fits launch week: the Rider Guide already centers the in-cabin screen, Musk teased PlayStation/Xbox plugs, and Tesla has talked theater, gaming, and upcoming V5 Starlink for the cabin. Voice via Grok is how they want riders to get that off the glass while the car drives. Pair it with Monday morning's Electrek skeptic piece on fleet-sale economics.

stories.headline: Electrek: if a Cybercab fleet were profitable, Tesla wouldn't sell you one
stories.why_read: This-morning HN/Electrek counter to the owner-earnings pitch — MisterGreen's $40M wreck as the case study.
body: Electrek's September 7 piece says Tesla is circulating an interest form for businesses to buy and operate Cybercab fleets on its network — the same 2019 Autonomy Day pitch of ~$30,000 a year gross profit per vehicle. The tell, they argue: if running those fleets printed money, Tesla would keep every car. Selling you the asset means you eat capex and depreciation while Tesla keeps software margin and the network cut.

The cautionary tale is MisterGreen, a Dutch leasing firm that bought more than 4,000 Teslas on residual-value and robotaxi-income assumptions, then went bankrupt in December 2025 and wiped out bondholders — about $40 million lost after Tesla price cuts. Treat this as Electrek's thesis, not Tesla guidance. It is the skeptic foil to Dave Lee's overnight product-strategy thread.

stories.headline: Developers are baking off GPT-6 Astra vs Claude Fable 5.1 — speed vs reliability
stories.why_read: Fresh X news: Astra often finishes in ~1/3 the time and fewer tokens; Fable still wins some coding/knowledge work.
body: X news summaries this morning cluster around head-to-head tests of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (September 3) against Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 (September 1). Users report Astra finishing some tasks in about one-third the time with far fewer tokens — one cited example is 21K versus 64K — while Fable is still preferred for certain coding and knowledge-work jobs at $10 / $50 per million tokens.

Preferences vary by task, reasoning settings, and cost. It is the practical companion to the Plus rollout lead: the model is landing in more hands, and the routing question (when to pay for Astra) is no longer theoretical.

stories.headline: Caltech Mathathon: 40 hours, $2M+ in AI credits, solve an open problem
stories.why_read: HN this morning: first hackathon devoted to research-level mathematics — pinned-post physics/math amplifier.
body: Caltech is hosting what it calls the first hackathon ever devoted to research-level mathematics: October 30–November 1, a hundred teams given frontier models to attack open conjectures, then defend the results in front of leading mathematicians. The page leads with '40 hours, $2M+ AI credits, solve an open problem.'

The organizers cite three 2026 AI-math headlines as the reason: Erdős's planar unit-distance conjecture disproved (May 20, open 80 years), the first explicit non-sofic group (August 1, open 27 years), and a claimed complex structure on the six-sphere (August 23, open 78 years, marked unverified). Treat those as the organizers' citations. This is the Fermat-in-Lean beat turning into a spectator sport.

stories.headline: vLLM speculative decoding on AMD GPUs — DFlash hits ~2.87× on Gemma 4
stories.why_read: HN this morning; chips-and-inference taste: MTP, EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark on MI300X/MI355X.
body: The vLLM blog walks speculative decoding — draft then verify — across five methods (native MTP, Gemma 4 MTP, EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark) on AMD Instinct MI300X and MI355X with ROCm. The headline result in their sweep: DFlash reached 2.87× throughput versus the non-speculative baseline on gemma-4-26B-A4B-it / MATH500; Gemma 4 MTP hit 2.83× on the same target. Several combinations were near 1× or below baseline.

The practical point is that num_speculative_tokens is a workload knob, not a free lunch: later draft positions often stop paying for themselves. For a desk that lives on open-source inference, this is the AMD/ROCm serving card next to Astra's API price sheet.

stories.headline: Ask HN: Fable reverse-engineered a player-piano DRM — can I ship the decoder?
stories.why_read: HN ~229: Astra+Fable decoded PianoDisc's decoy-note obfuscation. Classic agent-meets-systems ethics.
body: jmpman asked HN whether he can publish what Claude Fable built after he fed it a PianoDisc Prodigy mp3. The right channel carries MIDI as a 2004.5 Hz square wave; Fable spotted decoy notes that make naive MIDI extracts unplayable on other systems, then wrote a Python encoder and a decoder that strips them. The thread sits around 229 points and 136 comments.

He got there by bouncing Astra and Fable on Gymnopédie No. 1 — rubato, solenoid timing, sustain — then asking Fable to compare his paid file against Mutopia. Treat the format details as the poster's report. It is the 'agents will ignore your DRM' story without another model card.

stories.headline: X news: Cybercab hard-brakes for a jaywalker near Congress Avenue
stories.why_read: This morning's cluster — a real-street edge case on the new Austin public fleet.
body: An X news summary circulating Monday describes a Cybercab around 10 a.m. on September 6 near Congress Avenue hitting a green light with a stopped car, then a pedestrian darting into the crosswalk. The write-up credits brake-by-wire with an immediate full stop and antilock without hydraulic lines. Some praise the reaction; others ask whether it should have slowed earlier.
Treat this as a social/news-cluster report, not Tesla telemetry. It is the safety beat beside the Grok-cabin lead and Electrek's fleet-economics skeptic.
